title: Scaled Rademacher entry is sub-Gaussian
statement: Fix natural numbers $k > 0$ and $d$, a vector $x \in \bbr^d$, a row index $i$, and a column index $j$. Consider the joint Rademacher product measure on the space of $k \times d$ real arrays $\omega = (\omega_{ij})$, under which every entry is an independent $\pm 1$ Rademacher variable (equal to $-1$ or $+1$ with probability $\tfrac12$ each). Then the scaled entry $\omega \mapsto (x_j/\sqrt{k})\,\omega_{ij}$ has a sub-Gaussian moment generating function with variance proxy $x_j^2/k$; that is, its moment generating function is finite and satisfies \[ \E\!\left[\exp\!\big(t\,(x_j/\sqrt{k})\,\omega_{ij}\big)\right] \le \exp\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\,\frac{x_j^2}{k}\,t^2\right) \qquad\text{for all } t \in \bbr. \]
hypotheses_covered: x is a vector in ℝ^d
row index i in Fin k
column index j in Fin d
joint Rademacher product measure on k×d arrays
variance proxy equal to x_j^2 / k
replaced:
For $k > 0$, $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and indices $i,j$, the function
$\omega \mapsto (x_j / \sqrt{k})\,\omega_{ij}$ satisfies
$\mathrm{HasSubgaussianMGF}(\cdot, x_j^2/k, \mathrm{radJointMeasure})$.
